title: Quarterly roadmap: Dedicated capacity bursting & autoscale strategy
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Objective: define and commit to a quarterly roadmap that enables predictable reserved capacity with a controlled bursting layer and autoscaling policies for Dedicated customers. Deliverables include a commercial bursting/pricing model, autoscale policy primitives, rollout plan for existing customers, dashboarding for cost/latency, and success metrics tied to OKRs (throughput per $, p95 latency, and SLA availability). This ticket scopes the PM-level plan, cross-functional milestones, and artifacts to hand to Eng/Design/Finance for execution.
acceptance_criteria: Pricing model for bursting approved by Finance and Legal (doc + example invoices)
Autoscale policy primitives defined (thresholds, cooldowns, burst cap) with API schema and config options
Prototype autoscale behavior validated on staging with representative workloads and documented performance trade-offs
Rollout-runbook and customer communication templates prepared for 3 pilot accounts
Dashboard and alert definitions (cost per 1M tokens, reserved utilization, burst usage) live in Console staging
OKR targets defined: reduce unit cost for burst-eligible workloads by 12% while maintaining p95 latency within SLA
updates: 2026-01-27: Kickoff with Eng infra, Finance, and Solutions — aligned on goals and data sources for forecasting.
2026-02-03: Collected historical dedicated usage from billing pipeline; initial analysis shows 18% of peak is short-duration spikes across top 40 customers.
2026-02-12: Product/Design workshop produced two UX flows: per-pool burst budgets and account-level burst toggles. Design asked for clearer failure state handling.
2026-02-20: Eng outlined autoscale primitives: headroom threshold, burst token bucket, cooldown window. Identified need for KV cache migration before enabling burst on some models (ENG-3897).
2026-02-28: Finance requested a conservative pricing band and example TCO for a 6-month pilot. Created revenue impact projection (see links).
2026-03-05: PM review with GTM — agreed on pilot segmentation and success thresholds. Decided to target mid-market customers first.
2026-03-10: Draft PRD published; next steps: design wireframes, eng tech spec, and legal review of T&Cs for burst billing.
notes: Rationale: Many Dedicated customers want predictable committed spend but need short-term headroom for traffic spikes. A bursting layer lets us sell smaller reserved pools with lower committed cost and pay-for-use burst on top.
Key trade-offs: exposing too much burst increases unit cost and billing complexity; too little burst erodes product ROI for customers. Need a simple pricing surface and guardrails.
Open question: should burst be priced as a premium per-token multiplier or as hourly burst capacity? Finance preference leans to per-token for transparency.
Operational constraints: burst billing must be attributable to tokens and route-level usage to avoid disputes. Billing pipeline changes required (ENG-4011).
Pilot criteria: 3 customers (one SaaS, one marketplace, one GPT-like app) with predictable baseline and measurable spikes.
